title: Standard Form: Writing, Ordering and Calculating
seo_title: Year 8 Standard Form Worksheets: Large and Small Numbers, Converting, Multiplying and Dividing
standard_text: Interpret and compare numbers in standard form A × 10ⁿ, 1 ≤ A < 10, where n is a positive or negative integer or zero.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 standard form worksheets: write large and small numbers in standard form, convert back to ordinary numbers, order numbers, and multiply and divide in standard form. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Standard form is A × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ A < 10. Big numbers have positive n, small numbers negative n.
key_sub: To multiply, multiply the front numbers and add the powers. Then adjust so the front number is between 1 and 10.
body_html:
How it works

A number in standard form is written as A × 10n, where 1 ≤ A < 10 and n is a whole number. Large numbers have a positive power; small numbers (less than 1) have a negative power.

To multiply, multiply the front numbers and add the powers. To divide, divide the front numbers and subtract the powers. Then adjust if the front number is not between 1 and 10.

Example

Write 4,700,000 in standard form.

4.7, and the point moves 6 places.

Answer: 4.7 × 106

Example

Write 0.00052 in standard form.

5.2, and the point moves 4 places to the right.

Answer: 5.2 × 10−4

Example

Work out (5 × 103) × (4 × 106).

5 × 4 = 20 and 3 + 6 = 9.

20 × 109 = 2 × 1010.

Answer: 2 × 1010

Common mistakes

  • Counting the zeros instead of the places the point moves: 4,700,000 is 4.7 × 106, not 105.
  • Using a positive power for a small number: 0.00052 = 5.2 × 10−4.
  • Leaving the front number too big: 20 × 109 should be 2 × 1010.
  • Ordering by the front number only: 9 × 103 is smaller than 1 × 104.

faq.a: A way of writing very large or very small numbers as A × 10ⁿ, where A is at least 1 and less than 10.

faq.q: How do I write a small number in standard form?
faq.a: Move the decimal point to after the first non-zero digit. Count the places moved, and use a negative power: 0.00052 = 5.2 × 10⁻⁴.

faq.q: How do I multiply numbers in standard form?
faq.a: Multiply the front numbers and add the powers of 10. If the front number becomes 10 or more, adjust: 20 × 10⁹ = 2 × 10¹⁰.

faq.q: How do I compare numbers in standard form?
faq.a: Compare the powers of 10 first. Only if they are the same, compare the front numbers.

items.q: Work out (2 × 102) ÷ (2 × 100). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Divide the front numbers: 2 ÷ 2 = 1. Subtract the powers: 2 − 0 = 2. 1 × 102.

items.q: Work out (2.4 × 103) × (9 × 10−3). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 2.4 × 9 = 21.6. Add the powers: 3 + (−3) = 0. 21.6 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust: 2.16 × 101.

items.q: Work out (4 × 105) ÷ (4 × 104). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Divide the front numbers: 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Subtract the powers: 5 − 4 = 1. 1 × 101.

items.q: Work out (1 × 108) × (3 × 10−1). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 1 × 3 = 3. Add the powers: 8 + (−1) = 7. 3 × 107.

items.q: Work out (1 × 107) × (8 × 100). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 1 × 8 = 8. Add the powers: 7 + 0 = 7. 8 × 107.

items.q: Work out (7 × 108) × (3 × 10−3). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 7 × 3 = 21. Add the powers: 8 + (−3) = 5. 21 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust: 2.1 × 106.

items.q: Work out (4.9 × 103) × (3 × 102). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 4.9 × 3 = 14.7. Add the powers: 3 + 2 = 5. 14.7 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust: 1.47 × 106.

items.q: Work out (8.75 × 10−3) ÷ (5 × 105). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Divide the front numbers: 8.75 ÷ 5 = 1.75. Subtract the powers: −3 − 5 = −8. 1.75 × 10−8.

items.q: Work out (9.1 × 104) × (6 × 102). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 9.1 × 6 = 54.6. Add the powers: 4 + 2 = 6. 54.6 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust: 5.46 × 107.

items.q: Work out (3.2 × 107) × (3 × 10−3). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 3.2 × 3 = 9.6. Add the powers: 7 + (−3) = 4. 9.6 × 104.

items.q: Work out (8.75 × 10−3) ÷ (5 × 101). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Divide the front numbers: 8.75 ÷ 5 = 1.75. Subtract the powers: −3 − 1 = −4. 1.75 × 10−4.

items.q: Work out (7 × 101) ÷ (4 × 101). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Divide the front numbers: 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75. Subtract the powers: 1 − 1 = 0. 1.75 × 100.

items.q: Work out (6 × 107) × (1 × 10−3). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 6 × 1 = 6. Add the powers: 7 + (−3) = 4. 6 × 104.

items.q: Work out (7.4 × 102) × (8 × 101). Give your answer in standard form.
items.e: Multiply the front numbers: 7.4 × 8 = 59.2. Add the powers: 2 + 1 = 3. 59.2 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust: 5.92 × 104.

items.q: The distance from the Earth to the Sun is about 150,000,000 km. Write this in standard form.
items.e: Move the point 8 places: 1.5 × 108 km.

items.q: A grain of sand has a mass of about 0.00006 g. Write this in standard form.
items.e: The 6 is 5 places after the point: 6 × 10−5 g.

items.q: The population of the UK is about 6.8 × 10<sup>7</sup>. Write this as an ordinary number.
items.e: Move the digits 7 places to the left: 68,000,000.

items.q: A virus is 1.2 × 10<sup>−7</sup> m long. Write this as an ordinary number.
items.e: Move the digits 7 places to the right: 0.00000012 m.

items.q: Light travels about 3 × 10<sup>5</sup> km every second. How far does it travel in 2 × 10<sup>3</sup> seconds?
Which number is NOT written in standard form?
items.e: The front number must be at least 1 and less than 10. 12 is too big, so 12 × 104 is not in standard form.

items.q: Mars is 2.28 × 10<sup>8</sup> km from the Sun. Jupiter is 7.78 × 10<sup>8</sup> km. How much further is Jupiter?
items.e: The powers are the same, so subtract the front numbers: 7.78 − 2.28 = 5.5. Answer 5.5 × 108 km.

items.q: Work out (4 × 10<sup>3</sup>) + (5 × 10<sup>2</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
An atom has a diameter of 1 × 10<sup>−10</sup> m. How many atoms side by side make 1 mm (1 × 10<sup>−3</sup> m)?

items.e: The most negative power of 10 is the smallest: 9 × 10−4 = 0.0009.

items.q: A hard drive holds 2 × 10<sup>12</sup> bytes. A photo uses 4 × 10<sup>6</sup> bytes. How many photos fit?
What is 10<sup>5</sup> as an ordinary number?
items.e: 1 followed by 5 zeros: 100,000.

items.q: The mass of the Earth is about 5.97 × 10<sup>24</sup> kg. The Moon is about 7.35 × 10<sup>22</sup> kg. Which is heavier?
items.e: 1024 is 100 times 1022, so the Earth is much heavier.
